After both halves land, this test can only be written by patching away one fix to verify the buggy behavior of the other — a tautological self-authored oracle: you artificially create the broken state and then assert it behaves brokenly, locking mock internals rather than production behavior into the suite.

Approach: 'Nothing in the store vocabulary changes, so no migration and no compatibility gate are involved' (this statement is about store vocabulary, not about existing identity records)
ABSENCE: no explicit statement that DC was not configurable in production before this story, which would justify no migration
findings.finding: The plan changes `apply_inbound_records.py` behavior from a silent no-op (DC assignees never have identity minted due to the `accountId` guard) to an active mint, and states 'no migration and no compatibility gate are involved.' However, it does not explicitly justify why no rollback or migration is needed for any existing DC inbound records that were processed under the old no-op behavior — relying implicitly on 'DC was not configurable until this story' without stating it. Under T4, a behavior change affecting existing records requires an explicit rollback/migration justification, not just acknowledgement.
findings.location: Scope section ('apply_inbound_records.py'); Approach ('no migration and no compatibility gate are involved')
scenarios: A team that used an earlier experimental DC configuration (before the schema widening) ran inbound passes that silently skipped identity minting; after this fix, a subsequent inbound pass may attempt to mint identities for records that already exist in a partial state, or may produce duplicates if any manual workarounds were applied.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Approach section: 'No migration is needed because `jira-datacenter` was rejected at config-load before this story's schema widening lands, so no production inbound pass has ever executed under the DC backend; the behavior change from silent-skip to active-mint therefore affects no existing records.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the `RemoteRef.instance` deferral decision — including the mutable-base-URL re-identification risk — in an ADR update or AGENTS.md note, so the constraint survives beyond the filed ticket.
evidence: 'RemoteRef is never constructed in production code … asserting it would require building that machinery — a different story, filed as [rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]'
'the design question (deriving instance from a mutable base URL silently re-identifies every ticket when an operator moves the instance)'
No mention of updating ADR 0035, AGENTS.md, or any design doc with this decision
findings.finding: The `RemoteRef.instance` architectural deferral is explicitly acknowledged as a gap (AC item, ticket [rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e], design question about deriving instance from a mutable base URL), but the plan mentions no ADR update, AGENTS.md note, or design-doc entry capturing the decision. A future implementer discovering that `RemoteRef.instance` is always empty in production code has no authoritative document explaining why.
findings.location: AC section — 'The `RemoteRef.instance` half of this criterion is deliberately NOT asserted here'; Scope section referencing [rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]
scenarios: A future developer adds `RemoteRef` construction to the reconcile path without realising the mutable-base-URL re-identification risk, because there is no ADR capturing why it was deferred and what the constraint is.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief ADR addendum to ADR 0035 (or a new ADR) documenting: (1) `RemoteRef.instance` is intentionally not populated until the derivation question is resolved, (2) the constraint that prevents a naive `base_url`-derived value, and (3) the ticket reference. A one-paragraph note in AGENTS.md cross-referencing [rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e] would also suffice.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Expand the story title (or add a prominent summary sentence at the top of the plan) to explicitly name the `apply_inbound_records.py` identity-minting fix as co-equal scope alongside the backend contract work, so reviewers and approvers cannot miss it.
evidence: Title: 'J7 — assemble JiraDataCenterBackend and hold it to the backend contract suite'
Scope entry: 'src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py — the inbound identity path derives BOTH the identity provider and its creation channel from the backend's vendor string'
AC: 'an inbound apply under the DC backend MINTS a ghost identity for a DC-shaped assignee (one with name and NO accountId), asserted by a test that FAILS against today's code'

AC: 'a test pins the compound failure: with the accountId guard fixed but the channel NOT mapped, the mint raises ValueError: invalid creation_channel jira-datacenter and that exception is SWALLOWED at DEBUG'
The plan itself acknowledges the expansion: 'Folded in from bug [rebar:5f48-244c-7063-42d0]'
findings.finding: The plan's body scope materially exceeds its title. The title promises 'assemble JiraDataCenterBackend and hold it to the backend contract suite', but the plan also fixes inbound identity minting in `apply_inbound_records.py` (a reconciler-core file, not the backend adapter) and pins a compound channel-mapping defect with multiple ACs. A reviewer or approver reading only the title will scope this story too narrowly and may not allocate review attention to the reconciler-core changes or to the two identity-related ACs that require RED-first test discipline.
findings.location: Title vs. Scope section / `apply_inbound_records.py` subsection and AC items for identity minting
scenarios: A reviewer approving this story based on its title allocates no review attention to `apply_inbound_records.py` and misses the dual-defect identity fix, leaving the compound failure unreviewed and potentially unmerged.

An executor reading only the title and AC list skips the compound-failure AC (believing it is bookkeeping) and ships the `accountId` guard fix alone, converting a silent no-op into a swallowed `ValueError` — the exact failure mode the plan warns against.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to: 'J7 — Assemble JiraDataCenterBackend, hold it to the backend contract suite, and fix DC inbound identity minting' — or add a one-sentence scope summary immediately after the title: 'This story has two co-equal deliverables: (1) making JiraDataCenterBackend satisfy the Backend port and pass the contract suite; (2) fixing apply_inbound_records.py to mint ghost identities for DC-shaped assignees under the shared jira channel.'

findings.finding: The Testing section describes positive capability `isinstance` checks (SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, SupportsAbsenceProbe) as planned work, but no AC item requires or verifies them — they are described deliverables without a covering criterion.

findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC5 to read: 'a test asserts the backend IS an instance of `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and is NOT an instance of `SupportsIncremental`.'
